subject: 3B57EEE27265EC0B9258A2C095E271E7
introduction: This guide is a collection of dream reports: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá dreaming of a cottage by Tiberias, of a runaway camel, of His Father commanding “Destroy this room”; believers who met in dreams those they would later serve; the Báb’s vision of the head of the Imám Ḥusayn; a prisoner’s dream on the morning of his execution; a father’s dream of his daughter’s illness. Some are treated as guidance, some simply told. Scripture is full of the same: Jacob’s ladder, Joseph’s stars, Solomon at Gibeon, Daniel before the king, Paul’s man of Macedonia, Pilate’s wife, and in the Qur’an Abraham’s dream and the Prophet’s. Scripture also doubts: Sirach compares the one who regards dreams to one catching at a shadow, and Jeremiah separates the dreamer’s dream from the word as chaff from wheat. Aristotle called fulfilled dreams coincidences, Mercutio “children of an idle brain”, Freud wishes; and Homer’s Penelope, with her gates of horn and ivory, admits that some mean something and that one cannot easily tell which.
questions: Which dreams in the guide change what someone does, and which are simply remembered? What marks the difference?
Jacob “observed the saying”; Jeremiah says to tell a dream as a dream. What stance toward one’s own dreams do these suggest, and does the guide’s arc agree?
Sirach, Aristotle and Mercutio dismiss dreams; Job’s Elihu says God “speaketh” in them. Can both be right? About the same dreams?
Abraham acted on a dream at great cost; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá was told in one to destroy a room. What would make it right, or wrong, to act on a dream?
Why do so many of these dreams bring the dreamer into the presence of someone who has died or is far away?

outside.why: A dream of a happy cottage by the lake of Tiberias. When the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream; then was our mouth filled with laughter.
Words given by the Prophet in a dream. Elihu in Job: God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not; in a dream, in a vision of the night, he openeth the ears of men.
“I revealed myself to thee in the world of vision.” If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
Seen in vision standing before the Lord and addressed. In Gibeon the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and said, Ask what I shall give thee.
A star and a circle of fire seen in prayer, taken as a spiritual disclosure. Jacob dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven.
Two stars seen over the place where a temple would rise. Joseph’s dream had stars too: the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.
His brothers envied him for it; but his father observed the saying. Jacob neither believes nor dismisses the dream; he keeps it in mind. Is that the attitude the readings recommend?
Seen in a dream in America, answering that God had brought her there. A vision appeared to Paul in the night: a man of Macedonia, saying, Come over and help us; and they went.
A dream whose memory has uplifted the soul. Your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions.
A widow tells her dream to a teacher, who interprets it. Joseph in prison: do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.
The Báb dreamed that an Imam gave Him sweets, and knowledge followed. God gave the four youths knowledge and skill; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
A dream of standing in a great mosque with people flocking in. The Qur’an of Muhammad’s dream of entering the Sacred Mosque: Allah hath fulfilled the vision for His messenger in very truth.

“Destroy this room”, commanded in a dream. Abraham says to his son: I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee; and the son: do that which thou art commanded. The Qur’an calls it a clear test. When is a dream a command?

A runaway camel in the desert: one of the guide’s ordinary dreams. Mercutio would say they are all such: dreams are the children of an idle brain, begot of nothing but vain fantasy. What distinguishes, in these accounts, a dream that means something?
A dream of a cannon in a street of ‘Akká, afterwards thought significant. Aristotle held that most dreams said to come true are to be classed as mere coincidences. How would one tell?

A fellow prisoner in chains wakes the others before dawn with his dream, and goes to his death rejoicing. The apostles, threatened: they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and spake the word of God with boldness.
A vision of scripture written over the Shah’s seat. Daniel reads a king his own dream: thou art this head of gold; and after thee shall arise another kingdom.
A dream of standing on the field of Karbilá. Before Gideon’s battle a soldier tells his fellow a dream of a barley loaf that overturned a tent, and Gideon takes heart.
A mother dreams of her last son with a dagger in his heart. Pilate’s wife: have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
Simeon to another mother: yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also.
Ten nights in the cave of Ḥirá, the sea of outpourings surging. Paul: caught up into paradise, he heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.

Answering in a dream state. Prospero: we are such stuff as dreams are made on, and our little life is rounded with a sleep. Several readings treat dreaming as a second world; Prospero treats waking as a first dream. What follows from each?

“In that very moment I recognized my Imam.” Penelope says dreams come through two gates: those through ivory are fatuous, those through horn mean something to those that see them. She does not say how to know the gate.
A night vision of the Holy Land raised into the air before a book was written. I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven.

A father away from home dreams his daughter is ill. Freud’s thesis was that a dream is the fulfilment of a wish; a dream like this one, of fear for a child, is the kind his critics put to him. What account of dreaming do the guide’s own narrators assume?
Scripture itself has the sceptic’s voice: whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind.

A dream about America told at morning tea, and a lesson drawn. Jeremiah’s rule: the prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that hath my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat?

shortfall: A few of the reports are single sentences about dreams of Bahá’u’lláh or of a departed friend whose content is not told; these were read with the companions of the fuller accounts beside them.
